executive_briefing: The focus of the AI narrative has shifted decisively from conversational interfaces toward autonomous agentic systems. Major enterprise players including Salesforce, Microsoft, and AWS are now aligning on a definition of 'Autonomous Agents' that prioritizes reasoning, planning, and independent task execution over simple response generation. This transition marks the 'next wave' of AI, where agents move beyond human-in-the-loop dependencies to operate as persistent, purposeful entities in secure business environments.

trends.name: Autonomous Agentic Reasoning & Planning
trends.summary: AI agents are evolving into systems capable of high-level goal decomposition through reasoning and planning rather than just pattern matching.
trends.evidence: NVIDIA and AWS define agents by their ability to autonomously reason, plan, and execute tasks in tandem with or on behalf of humans.

trends.name: Enterprise Agentic Orchestration
trends.summary: Large-scale deployment of autonomous agents within corporate frameworks to handle complex business logic without constant oversight.
trends.evidence: Salesforce (Agentforce) and Microsoft (Copilot) are marketing autonomous agents as a means to improve business efficiency and error reduction.

trends.name: Multi-Metric Model Economics
trends.summary: Shift in model evaluation from raw intelligence to a holistic view including price, tokens per second, latency, and context window efficiency.
trends.evidence: Leaderboards are now ranking models across complex vectors like TTFT (Time to First Token) and output speed alongside traditional accuracy metrics.

trends.name: Open-Weights LLM Proliferation
trends.summary: Increasing market share and developer interest in models with available weights like LLaMA and Mistral, challenging closed-source dominance.
trends.evidence: Historical growth of weights-available models since 2022 has created a competitive ecosystem for deployment and fine-tuning.

trends.name: Self-Learning Autonomous Intelligence
trends.summary: Development of agents that utilize self-supervised learning on vast datasets to improve performance without explicit human labeling.
trends.evidence: LLMs are increasingly trained using self-supervised learning on vast amounts of text, forming the foundation for adaptive agentic systems.
